business_problem: Eni needed to make multilingual subsurface documents and extracted scientific data usable across geoscience teams, but its relational platform struggled with hundreds of thousands of documents, terabytes of unstructured content, and the complexity of creating comprehensive, searchable datasets for global research and drilling decisions.
solution_summary: Eni rebuilt its geoscience document platform on MongoDB Atlas with support from MongoDB Consulting. The new managed document data platform ingests processed text, tables, images, metadata, and AI-enriched outputs from subsurface documents, then exposes that information through search, dashboards, and custom applications used by geologists, engineers, and drilling teams. Atlas Search helps users filter relevant documents across years and geographies, while Atlas Charts gives non-developers a code-free way to visualize unstructured data in dashboards instead of exporting CSVs and spreadsheets. Atlas fits Eni's multi-cloud strategy and simplifies security, encryption, deduplication, scaling, and routine maintenance. The result is a shared knowledge environment that shortens development work, improves data completeness for research decisions, and provides the document foundation for NLP and generative-AI services that answer questions with grounded scientific context.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Acts as the managed document data platform for extracted geoscience content, metadata, and application data.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Search
solution_components.role: Lets scientists find relevant records across large multilingual document collections using a Google-like interface.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Charts
solution_components.role: Provides code-free dashboards and visualizations over unstructured and extracted data.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Consulting
solution_components.role: Supported Eni's migration, training, and architecture choices for the new platform.

data_flow: Geoscience documents are extracted and enriched with AI, stored in Atlas as text, tables, images, and metadata, surfaced through Search and Charts for specialists and analysts, and fed into NLP and generative-AI services that retrieve relevant documents before answering questions.
business_outcome: Eni improved platform performance and manageability, reduced development time and associated costs, gave scientists faster access to comprehensive subsurface datasets, and created a cloud-agnostic document platform that can support broader enterprise rollout and future generative-AI enhancements.
architecture_clues: The platform stores text, tables, images, and metadata extracted from documents.
Atlas Charts is used alongside Power BI to visualize unstructured data with minimal coding.
Eni currently uses generative AI to retrieve relevant documents and uses LLMs to build answers.
evidence_quotes: Eni’s document management platform for geosciences offers an ecosystem of services and applications for creating and sharing content.
MongoDB Atlas is simple to integrate and makes it easy to ingest and deduplicate data from other systems.
Atlas Charts is really useful to visualize unstructured data.
The generative AI we’ve introduced currently creates vector embeddings from documents, so when a user asks a question, it retrieves the most relevant document and uses LLMs to build the answer.
